analysis.title: Global Economic Weekly: Walls of worry
key_insights: BofA says investors increasingly doubt the AI trade is sustainable. Capex keeps surprising to the upside, which raises the odds of a slowdown if profits do not keep pace. A correction in the AI trade is called probably the number one risk for the global economy.
An AI correction would slow US capex and Asian exports sharply. It could also hit US consumption through lost equity wealth effects.

Tighter global financial conditions are a second first-order risk. Higher real rates partly reflect heavy debt supply to fund AI investment and large fiscal deficits. Regions without an AI capex or export boom, such as Europe, are hit hardest.

France is the weak link. French yields are at levels last seen in the Eurozone crisis. BofA thinks the ECB's pain threshold for intervening is much higher than markets would like. If contagion grows, intervention becomes more likely.

BofA argues the Fed is behind the curve. US GDP growth is strong and spreading beyond AI capex, price pressures are broadening, and inflation has been above target for six years. BofA says Warsh missed a chance to build credibility by hiking at this meeting.
BofA's new Fed call is 50bp of additional hikes at a quarterly cadence, in December and March. The Fed upper bound is now 4.00%, with a forecast of 4.25% by Nov-26 and 4.50% by Mar-27.

Geopolitics adds caution. BofA cites reported high chances of Iran escalation after the US midterms. Oil prices bottom at a higher floor after each escalation spike, which supports more persistent inflation.

US midterms are not expected to change BofA's economic outlook through 2028. The baseline is a split Congress with gridlock, deficits near 6% of GDP, and a Republican sweep adding 10-20bp to growth in each of two years via defense spending.

The administration is expected to pivot toward foreign policy, trade and deregulation, where executive authority matters. This could bring bouts of policy uncertainty, but far smaller than after Liberation Day.

AI regulation is a state and local issue over the next two years, not a federal one. State data-center legislation and local moratoriums are rising, but BofA sees them slowing construction at the margin rather than derailing the investment cycle.

ECB held rates with a hiking bias and added dovish language to the written statement. Lagarde said QT proceeds mechanically and the direction of travel is clear absent surprises. BofA still expects a December hike, perhaps another in March, but December is no longer a done deal.

ECB market pricing: about 3bp of the 74bp of hikes implied over the next year was priced out. December pricing rose to 22bp. BofA doubts the ECB can deliver the roughly 70bp priced, and prefers duration in the belly of the curve over the very front end.

A Reuters report cited ECB sources saying a December hike is all but certain barring a collapse in energy prices. The same sources expect a pause after December because higher bond yields could cut growth by 100bp and inflation by 90bp over 2027-28.

BofA expects the BoE to hike 25bps to 4.0% next week on a 7-2 vote, with Taylor and Dhingra dissenting. It sees a second hike in February to 4.25% and calls market pricing of four or more hikes excessive.

UK data was hawkish versus BoE forecasts: September headline CPI 3.5%, services CPI 3.7%, unemployment 4.7%. BofA expects the BoE to show an inflation peak of 4.2% in 2027Q1 and medium-term inflation unchanged at 1.9%.

New Zealand's 7 November election is a close race between Labour and National. The centrist Opportunity party is potentially pivotal. A Labour-led government would restore the RBNZ dual mandate, which would likely lower the market-implied OCR path.

Israel's election left neither bloc with 61 seats. The Netanyahu bloc is projected at 53, the Eisenkot bloc at 48 and Arab parties at 19. A unity government or another election in spring 2027 is possible. Macro read-through is limited, with the shekel the main channel.
Chile's central bank held at 4.5% with a net hawkish statement. BofA expects a hold in coming meetings and hikes of 50bp starting in 3Q27, since the economy is weak and underlying inflation is 3.2%.

Strait of Hormuz flows have largely normalized, but getting crude out is costlier than before the war.

tension_points.bull_case: Global activity remains resilient on AI-linked capex, and US growth is spreading beyond AI capex.
tension_points.bear_case: The more capex surprises up, the sooner a slowdown arrives if profitability lags. A correction would slow US capex and Asian exports and could spill over to the US consumer through wealth effects.

tension_points.bull_case: Lagarde said the direction of travel is clear absent surprises, and Reuters cited ECB sources calling a December hike all but certain barring a collapse in energy prices.
tension_points.bear_case: Dovish statement language, tight financial conditions and almost no second-round effects make a hold plausible, and BofA doubts the ECB can deliver the roughly 70bp priced.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Activity data deteriorating more than expected, financial conditions staying this tight, core inflation not moving much, and second-round effects not surprising.

tension_points.bull_case: Inflation is rising toward 4% in early 2027, growth and labor data are strong, and Bailey says a hike is getting harder to avoid.
tension_points.bear_case: Second-round effects are limited so far, medium-term inflation is forecast below 2%, and BofA sees four or more hikes as excessive.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Concrete evidence that strong second-round effects are materializing, which would be needed for the four-plus hikes the market prices.
